text:
maria: Heads-up: onboarding of gptx-3b-quant-v2 is failing. Staging load OOMs on rtx-a100 pool and we saw weird garbled tokens when traffic hit the dequant fallback in prod for a few requests. Can folks help triage?

kevin: where are the weights stored? s3 path and the model-registry manifest name pls.

maria: s3://redwood-models/gptx/gptx-3b-quant-v2/latest.tar.gz and manifest is models/gptx/gptx-3b-quant-v2/manifest.json in the registry. I pushed the package this morning.

kevin: checking… quick note: model manifest lists tokenizer: "bpe-bytechunk-v1" but the deployed tokenizer artifact in the package is sentencepiece.model. that mismatch could explain garbled tokens when fallback used.

sam: oncall saw the OOMs around 11:07 UTC on host r-a100-17 (pod inference-a100-7). logs show allocation spikes during shard load. reducing max_shard_size might help as a stopgap.

maria: paste of load error: ```2026-03-17T11:07:12Z ERROR loader: failed to allocate shard 0: CUDA out of memory (cuMemAlloc) size=12.3GB```

deploy-bot: deployment "gptx-3b-quant-v2" rolled out to staging at 2026-03-17T11:05:34Z (id: dpl_9876) :rocket:

nina: any customer impact? did prod traffic actually hit this model or just staging?

maria: prod had a small percent (5%) routed to the dequant variant during capacity fallback window; about 12 requests returned weird tokens like "�\u0000�" and one logged a generation mismatch. No data exfil.

kevin: action plan: 1) confirm tokenizer artifacts inside the tarball (tokenizer.json + vocab). 2) if mismatch, repack with correct bpe tokenizer from model-registry and upload. 3) add a manifest validation step to the registry CI so tokenizer type must match artifact.

sam: for immediate mitigation, I can scale down concurrency on the a100 pool and enable --loader-max-shard-size=8G for that deployment to avoid OOM while we repack.

maria: thanks. quick check: how do I inspect the tarball from CI? I used the publish job name "model-publish/gptx-3b-quant-v2" — any quick command?

kevin: you can run: ```aws s3 cp s3://redwood-models/gptx/gptx-3b-quant-v2/latest.tar.gz - | tar -tzf - | grep tokenizer``` to list contents. to extract run `aws s3 cp ... - | tar -xzf - -C /tmp/gptx` then inspect /tmp/gptx/tokenizer*

maria: ran that in a sandbox, found sentencepiece.model and no tokenizer.json. manifest indeed says bpe-bytechunk-v1. looks like publisher job used wrong tokenizer artifact.

kevin: I'll open a hotfix PR to replace the artifact and add CI validation. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/model-registry/pull/542 (adds tokenizer-type check + test).

maria: creating a repack and upload now, will trigger staging rollout and run smoke.

sam: I'll apply the loader flag to the staging deployment and throttle concurrency for the a100 pool for 30m.

nina: let me know if we should notify customers or if rollback is cleaner.

maria: if staging looks good I'll promote the fixed package and we can do a controlled roll to prod at low traffic. rollback not needed if we can replace quickly.

kevin: also recommend adding a quick preflight in the serving runtime to compare tokenizer.signature against model manifest and reject mismatches (error before serving). I can file an infra issue.

maria: filing a small follow-up ticket to add a preflight check and include a snippet for the team. thanks all :pray:
